subject: Request: architecture catalogue + isolation narrative for SOC 2 audit
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@veritas.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: veritas-security@veritas.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 evidence: high-level narrative + diagrams needed

Jordan —

Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. Veritas is kicking off a SOC 2 readiness review next week and our audit team asked for a concise package describing how Redwood separates tenant workloads at the network/data-plane level for both Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Specific asks: a one-page narrative we can hand to auditors, a pair of diagrams (Dedicated vs Private), a short table that maps SIG/CAIQ questions to concrete artifacts, and an XLS with evidence pointers.

Things that are blockers for us today:
- We need a clear description of how egress is controlled for Private deployments (who manages routing, where KMS keys live).
- For Dedicated, the auditor wants the isolation story from physical host -> service mesh -> tenant inference processes (high level is fine, but call out any shared components).

Can you send something by EOD Monday? If you prefer, an internal short-read + attachments is fine — our audit lead will take it from there.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Chen
Security Manager, Veritas Systems
emily.chen@veritas.com

Attachments: none

Hi Emily —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can do a compact package that includes: a one-page isolation narrative, two diagrams (SVGs) for Dedicated and Private, a mapping CSV that ties SIG/CAIQ questions to our artifacts, and a short spreadsheet with doc links and sample screenshots of console configs / telemetry. Kimberly will assemble the technical details; Ben will pull the organizational/ops playbook pieces (who owns what during an audit, SLAs for artifact delivery).

Plan:
- Kimberly: produce diagram + technical notes (policy, routing control, KMS residency, audit logs)
- Ben: produce ops playbook + evidence XLS (owners, sample artifacts, expected response times)
- Jordan: synthesize into a one-page narrative and a cover email for your auditors

We may ask you one clarifying Q about the scope (do auditors want examples of ephemeral file-system traces or just network/KMS/access control screenshots?).

Deliverables: redwood_isolation_catalogue_v1.pdf, diagram-dedicated-private-vpc.svg, MAP-tenant-fence-table.csv, sig-responses-veritas.xlsx. Will send first drafts within 6 hours and final package by 16:00 PDT.

Jordan Blake

Subject: Draft: technical notes + artifacts for Veritas SOC 2 pack

Emily / Jordan / Ben —

Attached are the first drafts (SVG + CSV + XLS referenced below). I focused the technical notes on the two deployment planes you requested and included explicit callouts for SIG/CAIQ controls we typically map. Summary highlights:

1) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — isolation narrative- Physical layer: Dedicated capacity is backed by reserved GPU pools (no cross-tenant scheduling on GPU hosts). We use hypervisor-level project isolation and process namespace isolation for inference runners.- Service plane: A multi-tenant control plane (separate from the inference host network) orchestrates model placement; for network traffic, each tenant inference process is bound to a tenant-specific overlay network (VLAN/segment) enforced by the host-level network agent.- Shared components and mitigations: logging/metrics collectors and edge TLS termination are shared; they run in separated namespaces with strict RBAC and mTLS to the control plane. We call out principle of least privilege and runtime seccomp profiles for inference processes.

2) Private (VPC / on-prem) — isolation narrative- Network boundary: Private deployments are provisioned into customer-managed VPCs (customer controls VPC routing and peering). For Redwood-managed Private (we manage control plane only), egress sits at a customer-configured edge (NAT gateway / firewall) — customers can route egress through their own transit networks or require us to push via an approved egress-hop.- KMS: By-default KMS keys for private deployments can be customer-provided (KMS in their cloud account) or, for managed KMS, keys live in Redwood's tenant-scoped KMS project with strict access control and audit logging. The mapping sheet explains which model to choose based on regulatory needs.

3) Egress controls & evidence pointers- Private: sample artifacts include VPC route tables screenshot (attachment: vpc-route-table-example.png), Cloud NAT settings screenshot (cloudnat-example.png), and a short runbook describing how to enforce egress-only service endpoints.- Dedicated: sample artifacts include host-level iptables config snippet (host-iptables.txt), overlay segment assignment CSV (MAP-tenant-fence-table.csv), and tenant binding logs showing network namespace assignment.

4) SIG / CAIQ mapping- I mapped a targeted subset of CAIQ items (Network Security, Boundary Definition, Key Management, Logging & Monitoring) to the deliverables in the attached XLS (sig-responses-veritas.xlsx). Each row points to the artifact, owner, and expected timestamp to produce during an audit.

Attachments included in this draft (stubs):
- diagram-dedicated-private-vpc.svg (diagram)
- MAP-tenant-fence-table.csv (segmentation mapping)
- sig-responses-veritas.xlsx (mapping + artifact pointers)
- redwood_isolation_catalogue_v1.pdf (one-page narrative draft)

Quick clarifying Qs for Veritas:
1) For Private deployments, do you need an example where the customer explicitly requires an air-gapped control plane? If so, we can add an airgap appendix that covers out-of-band update procedures.
2) For Dedicated, do auditors want host forensic traces (we can provide sanitized logs) or are configuration artifacts sufficient?

Jordan — I'll hand this to you to fold into the cover narrative. Ben — can you add the ops playbook paragraph for who owns evidence collection (CS vs infra vs security) and expected SLAs?

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments (referenced): diagram-dedicated-private-vpc.svg, MAP-tenant-fence-table.csv, sig-responses-veritas.xlsx, redwood_isolation_catalogue_v1.pdf

Kimberly / Jordan / Ben —

This is perfect and highly actionable, thank you. A few quick notes from the audit team after reviewing your draft attachments:

- Airgap appendix: yes, please include an airgap addendum. We have two regulated customers who will require the offboarded control plane option.
- Host traces: configuration artifacts and sanitized logs are sufficient for the readiness phase; we may ask for a short host-forensics sample later.
- KMS proof: example KMS key policy and an example audit log (redacted) would satisfy the Key Management control. If you can point us to a single example tenant where keys are customer-owned vs Redwood-managed, that would be ideal.

Next steps: when you push the final package, please include one consolidated PDF (redwood_isolation_catalogue_v1.pdf) and the SVG + CSV + XLS as separate files. We'll confirm receipt and provide any follow-ups.

Emily Chen
Security Manager, Veritas Systems
emily.chen@veritas.com
